analysis.title: Paul Donovan's daily audio: Five points
key_insights: US Democrats decisively won the midterm elections. State results matter because data center siting decisions often occur at state level and some Democratic governors publicly oppose them. Data center builders will likely have to offer more incentives to local communities.
Fiscal gridlock looks more likely after the federal results, which has supported US government bonds.
Trump's nominees are less likely to be confirmed, including any future vacant Federal Reserve governor seats.
Administration members will have to divert time to preparing for congressional hearings.
The Senate shift puts Democrats in a strong position in two years, when the available seats favor them. This matters for the next administration's legislative agenda.
Republican Party unity is of investor interest because Trump's personal endorsements did not translate into electoral success.

California ballot initiative results on the billionaires' tax are not yet known. The initiative is part of a global trend, alongside Italy's recently proposed wealth exit tax. Private wealth is at record highs and indebted governments will seek to mobilize it.
risk_factors: State-level opposition from some Democratic governors to data center projects, raising incentive costs for builders
Rising wealth taxation as indebted governments seek to mobilize record private wealth
